title: BrowserOS server route authentication hardening — Cycle 11 weak-spot closure
problem: BrowserOS exposed several internal HTTP sub-routers without enforcing the existing `requireTrustedAppOrigin()` middleware. The unprotected routes covered agent management (`/agents`), the SOUL registry (`/soul`), monitoring introspection (`/monitoring`), ACL policy (`/acl-rules`), and the Claw orchestrator (`/claw`). Any website or remote script that could reach the loopback port could invoke these administrative endpoints, allowing information disclosure or unauthorized control of the Trinity A2A runtime.
root_cause: `packages/browseros-agent/apps/server/src/api/server.ts` mounted each sub-application with `.route('/path', subApp)` but did not prepend `.use('/path/*', requireTrustedAppOrigin())`. The auth middleware was already implemented and used on chat/task routes, so the gap was purely an omission in router composition.
fix: Applied `requireTrustedAppOrigin()` to all administrative sub-routers in `server.ts` for `/agents`, `/soul`, `/monitoring`, `/acl-rules`, and `/claw`. Added a focused test file expansion in `tests/api/routes/auth-routes.test.ts` that mounts dummy protected sub-apps and asserts 403 for untrusted remote origins while preserving access for loopback no-Origin requests. Confirmed `bun tsc --noEmit` passes and the targeted auth test suite passes.

waivers: AGENT-V-WAIVER: browseros-ai/BrowserOS#2024 for hand-edited server.ts and auth-routes.test.ts
follow_up: Consider adding a central `adminRouter()` wrapper that automatically applies `requireTrustedAppOrigin()` so future sub-routers cannot be mounted without auth.
Extend the test suite to verify authenticated loopback/extension requests receive 200 from the real sub-routers once DB-free harness helpers are available.
Run the full server test suite (`bun test`) under a separate issue; several unrelated failures exist in browser-launch-args, build, and monitoring-service tests.
